title: Add lazy-index prefill skip and deferred-decode coalescer to reduce KV churn
author: Priya Nair
description:
Context: Our production traces show a class of short-lived prefill requests that perform expensive KV lookups to prime tiny token ranges, causing KV churn and adding tail latency for co-scheduled decodes. This PR introduces two cooperating mechanisms: (1) a lazy-index prefill path that opportunistically skips KV index lookups for prefill slices under a size threshold and instead tags them for on-demand KV priming during decode; and (2) a deferred-decode coalescer that batches those tagged slices with imminent decode work so we perform a single compacted KV read and a single small decode kernel invocation.

Goals: reduce KV system pressure, lower median and tail latency for mixed-length interactive workloads, and preserve quality by ensuring prefill correctness when full KV state is required.

Design summary:
- Lazy-index prefill: a new runtime flag and small codepath (lazy_index_hint) that short-circuits full index maintenance for slices < N tokens (configurable; default 8). Prefill requests marked lazy carry a lightweight tag in the request metadata rather than mutating global KV index state immediately.
- Deferred-decode coalescer: scheduler component that listens for lazy-tagged prefill completions and waits up to a short window (configurable default 6ms) to merge them with an upcoming decode from the same session/strand. When coalescing, the system issues one KV priming round and a coalesced decode kernel call that processes multiple tiny slices in a single micro-batch.
- Kernel interaction: added a small micro-batch path in the cuda kernel adapter to accept tightly-packed slices (same dtype/shape) to amortize kernel launch and memory crossing overhead. This path is guarded by the feature flag and fallbacks to the existing path for heterogeneous slices.
- Safety and correctness: lazy prefill maintains a tombstone/tag that guarantees that an eventual decode will trigger KV priming; strict asserts in dev mode ensure we never skip priming before consuming model attention.

Implementation notes:
- runtime/prefill/lazy_indexer.cpp: implements tagging and size-based decision logic.
- runtime/prefill/pipeline_coalescer.cc: coalescer state machine, windows, and eviction heuristics.
- runtime/scheduler/slice_coordinator.rs: scheduling hint plumbing and timing windows used by the coalescer.
- runtime/kernels/micro_batch_adapter.cu: micro-batch kernel entrypoint and safety checks.
- configs/feature_flags/prefill_lazyindex.yaml: feature gating and tuning knobs.
- tests/bench/bench_prefill_latency.py: benchmark harness added to reproduce latency numbers.
- docs/observability/prefill_metrics.md: new metrics and dashboard queries to track effectiveness.

Performance: On the interactive-chat benchmark (gpt-medium-like, mix of short prompts and longer contexts) toggling the new path with conservative default thresholds produced: median prefill-to-first-decode latency -7.1%, 95th percentile -12.8%, and KV read volume per 1k requests dropped ~9.3%. Micro-batching the tiny slices reduced kernel launch overhead for those cases by ~18%. Numbers vary by model shape and request mix; included benchmark outputs in the PR artifacts.

Feature flag and rollout: This is behind feature flag "prefill_lazy_index" in the control plane and default-off in canary clusters. Rollout plan: enable in a canary shard for 72h, monitor new metrics (prefill.lazy_skips, coalescer.coalesced_count, kv.read_bytes_delta, tail_latency), then expand to dedicated capacity clusters where we expect high short-prefill rates.

Testing and CI: added unit tests for the lazy index decision logic and integration bench that validates coalescing does not change token outputs for canonical prompts. Local microbench and GPU CI run green.

Notes and risks: the heuristics (slice-size threshold and coalescing window) are workload sensitive; default values chosen conservatively. We added safety telemetry to detect regressions in output quality. If significant output divergence is detected the flag can be auto-rolled back.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed by runtime and serving teams
- [x] Unit and integration tests added
- [x] Bench artifacts attached
- [x] Feature-flag gating and rollout plan included
- [x] Observability and alerts defined

Related: follows-up on ENG-1284 (prefill KV pressure analysis) and pairs with upcoming scheduler work to prioritize coalescing where decode latency budgets allow.

review_comments: Marcus Lee: Nice approach. Two questions: how do you guarantee idempotency for tags across retries? Could you add an e2e test that simulates prefill retry?
Priya Nair: Added a retry-safe tag GUID and new integration test retry_prefill_recovery in this branch (see tests/bench).
Elena Cruz: Kernel path looks fine but add a fallback assert that rejects heterogeneous shapes; also add a small knob to limit max coalesced slices per batch for memory safety.
Priya Nair: Added assertion and max_coalesce_slices configuration; bench runs unchanged.
Jonah Alvarez: CI lint failed on the first run due to header ordering in lazy_indexer.cpp. Fixed and pushed. Please verify metrics names align with observability conventions.
Priya Nair: Metrics renamed to prefilling.lazy_skips and coalescer.coalesced_count per review.
merge_meta: Merged by Elena Cruz (squash) on 2026-03-06. Merge commit message: 'feat(prefill): lazy-index skip + deferred decode coalescer (ENG-1284) - squash'
release_notes:
- Introduce lazy-index prefill path to avoid unnecessary KV index mutations for small prefill slices.
- Add deferred-decode coalescer to combine tiny prefill slices with decode work and reduce KV reads and kernel launches.
- Add micro-batch kernel adapter to amortize kernel overhead for compacted slices.
- Feature gated behind 'prefill_lazy_index' and default-off for canary rollout.
